findings.reason: the plan should extend `review.py`'s record store (generalise its keyed path/selection) rather than fork it, exactly the "state readers" duplicate the plan's own §3 rubric names, and the fork contradicts the reuse the decision claims.
findings.text: `_target_path`/`_stored_blob8`/`_candidate_paths`/`read_plan_review` re-implement, keyed on `plan_version`+blob8, exactly the "same key, second record of it moves to an `.at-<sha>` sibling, newest-by-mtime wins" selection that `reckon/crew/review.py` already owns as `_partial_review_path` (`review.py:1076`), `_complete_review_exists` (`review.py:1009`) and `stored_record` (`review.py:1444`); the plan's `review-storage` decision and D1 claim the store "reuses the code-review machinery", yet the selection logic is a parallel copy that will drift from the owner as the store's rules change

findings.reason: path resolution is the recurring duplicate the plan's own §3 rubric names, and the honest change is to name and call `resolve_resource` in the design rather than add a second resolution path.
findings.text: `plan_review_subject` resolves the plan document as `flight.mounted_project_docs()[project] / "plans" / f"{slug}.html"`, while `require_plan_reviewed` two functions away (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2665`) resolves the same plan through `resolve_resource`, the canonical resolver in `reckon/resources.py:557` that roadmap, evidence and resources.py also use; the sweep and the gate can therefore disagree about which plan a slug names (archived, migrated or colliding slugs) and the plan's design does not name one resolver

findings.reason: the plan should either add the interface-budget item to the rubric (extending `interface_counts` into it, as the §2 anchor item was folded in) or drop the "Also done when", because a done-when the named mechanism cannot produce is a criterion that can never be met.
findings.text: §3's interface-budget half ("the review cites the current week's four figures … a section that adds surface without naming what it retires or merges … receives a finding") is a declared done-when (`plan.html` §3, "Also done when") with no home in the delivered rubric: `plan_design_review.md` carries only the four depth items, `PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS` (`reckon/crew/review.py:157`) matches those four, and the composed brief adds nothing, so no plan review will ever emit the check the plan promises over `reckon/interface_counts.py`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` hides the record shape, the store, the content-join by fingerprint, the authored-prose digest and the report parser behind a small interface (`plan_fingerprint`, `store_plan_review`, `read_plan_review`, `unanswered_findings`, `record_response`), substantively more behaviour than it exposes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` forks the review store's file-selection and blob-keyed-sibling machinery that `reckon/crew/review.py` already owns, and the plan's own `review-storage` decision says it reuses that store; and `plan_review_subject` resolves the plan path by hand rather than through `reckon/resources.py::resolve_resource`, the resolver the gate two functions away already uses.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the review store, the review reflex, the refusal-family table, `_is_review_node`, `reckon/interface_counts.py` and the flight defaults as the machinery it extends, and each citation resolves.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 declares an interface-budget check (cite the week's four counts; retire-or-justify any added surface) that the delivered design rubric `reckon/crew/prompts/plan_design_review.md` does not carry and does not justify omitting, so the check exists only as plan prose over the existing `interface_counts` measurement.
